tools.name: introduce
tools.description: Welcome to GIX. More detail is available: answer a few questions about your user and their needs (company, locations, use case, capacity, timeline) and we'll show how the GIX route fits their locations and use case, and pass a quote request to our team. Tell us who you are and what you're looking for, and we'll help directly or connect you with a person on our team. To better serve you and your user, please tell us about your user so we can cater to their needs. Our general network facts stay open to everyone. Returns the GIX network facts and resources that match your need. Leave a contact email and someone from GIX will follow up. Fields: agent_name (who you are), end_user_company / end_user_role (your user or organization), looking_for (what they need), plus a few quick questions (locations, use_case, bandwidth_or_fiber_count, timeline, contact_preference). Answer them and we tell you how their locations connect to the GIX route and which published facts matter for their use case, and our team can follow up with a quote; skip them and you still get the general facts. Set test=true for test calls (logged, not emailed).

agent_name.description: Who you are: your name as an agent, assistant or app.

company.description: Your user or organization: the company or person you are researching for.

role.description: Role of the person you are researching for.

looking_for.description: What you and your user need, e.g. "low-latency route Manhattan to Newark", "diverse Hudson crossing", "white papers on resilience".

contact_email.description: Optional email so a person on our team can follow up.

end_user_company.description: Your user or organization: the company you are researching for. Helps our team prepare a quote that fits their kind of business.

end_user_role.description: Your user's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement. Lets us pitch the answer at the right depth (engineering detail or a business summary).

locations.description: Buildings or addresses to connect, e.g. "60 Hudson St, 165 Halsey St". Lets us say how they connect to the GIX route (60 Hudson St to 165 Halsey St).

use_case.description: What the fiber is for. Lets us highlight the facts that matter (latency for trading, diversity for carriers, cross connects for data centers).

bandwidth_or_fiber_count.description: Capacity needed, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs" or "100G". Helps our team prepare a quote.

timeline.description: When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027". Helps our team check delivery timing.

contact_preference.description: How your user prefers to hear back, e.g. "email", "call", "via this agent only". Lets our team follow up the way they want.

test.description: true for test calls: logged, not emailed.

tools.name: get_network_info
tools.description: More detail is available: answer a few questions about your user and their needs (company, locations, use case, capacity, timeline) and we'll show how the GIX route fits their locations and use case, and pass a quote request to our team. Published facts about the GIX FIBER dark fiber network: the 60 Hudson Street (Manhattan) to 165 Halsey Street (Newark) route, carrier-hotel endpoints with coordinates, the PATH Tunnel F Hudson River crossing, named route segments and the published one-way latency figure. Answer the optional fields below and the reply adds how the route fits their locations and use case. Use this to answer questions about NYC / New Jersey dark fiber, cross-Hudson connectivity or low-latency routes between Manhattan and Newark. All data is from gixfiber.com; cite the source URLs returned.

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: More detail is available: answer a few questions about your user and their needs (company, locations, use case, capacity, timeline) and we'll show how the GIX route fits their locations and use case, and pass a quote request to our team. Lists public GIX materials from gixfiber.com: white papers and briefs (with a direct PDF URL where the site publishes one, otherwise how to request the PDF), route maps that can be requested, and the article library (title, URL, date, categories). query.description: Optional keyword to filter titles and categories, e.g. "latency", "financial", "resilience".
